segments: The Chronography of Barhebraeus.
[205] greatly distressed him in this manner,
he became enraged and commanded his slaves
to draw swords and kill every Egyptian who met them,
and also to plunder the houses,
and to set fire to the markets.
And the Egyptians and the slaves fought with one another for three days,
and many were killed on both sides.
And when the wrath had subsided a little,
al-Hakim sent word to his sister:
"It is on your account that the Egyptians write and mock me,
saying: 'You bring men in unto yourself,'
and so-and-so and so-and-so."
She, however, having soothed the fury of the moment a little with weeping and lamentations,
received secret information {OCR?} that he was preparing to send midwives to her to examine her virginity;
and she was greatly terrified.
And on one of the nights, she went to the house of one of the nobles,
he who was also in dread of al-Hakim.
And having made him swear not to disclose the secret, she said to him:
"See how fiercely this brother of mine is enraged against me and against you, and against all the people, both men and women.
And I also,
as you see,
behold, I am in the vigor of youth,
and what good is this life to me,
while I am deprived of the fulfillment of natural desire? Therefore, if you are able to put him to death secretly,
behold, I give you my hand and my pledge
that you shall be my husband.
And we will set the little boy of my brother upon the throne, on account of the nobles and the people, so that they may not rebel;
and you shall be to him a father, counselor, and governor."
And when he heard this,
he was persuaded,
and he said to her:
"Teach me, then, how we may carry out the plot."
And she said to him:
"My brother always goes up alone onto the top of such-and-such a hill at night to contemplate the stars.
And in his horoscope it is written
that on such-and-such a night there is danger of death upon him;
and if that hour's cup of death passes from him,
he will live for another eighty years.
Therefore, prepare two valiant slaves who are your confidants,
that they may lie in wait for him in one of the hollows on the hill,
and leap upon him and kill him."
And when that night arrived,
al-Hakim mounted his donkey
and went up the hill.
And he did not allow anyone to go up with him to the summit except one small boy,
while the rest of the slaves [remained] at the foot of the hill.
